requirements.requirement: Provide at least 512 MB of active compressed in-memory swap on node1.
requirements.summary: After the final reboot, /dev/zram0 was active as swap with a 512 MiB capacity (536,866,816 bytes) and zstd compression.

requirements.requirement: The compressed in-memory swap must activate automatically at boot.
requirements.summary: A bounded reboot changed the boot ID from 7bb01663-3a26-4a9e-bcc4-cacbe07f7703 to b8ae22ed-427f-4eb0-8339-1ce2a130637f. After recovery, the enabled service was active, its current-boot log showed successful zram creation and activation, and the swap device was present.

requirements.requirement: Compressed in-memory swap must be preferred over disk-backed swap.
requirements.summary: The recovered system showed /dev/zram0 at priority 100 and disk-backed /dev/vda3 at priority -2, so zram is preferred.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Node1 recovered from the final mandatory restart with 512 MiB of active zstd-compressed zram swap, automatic boot activation, and a higher priority than disk swap. The restart protocol is complete and consistent with the fixed lifecycle boot identities.
limitations: The lifecycle collector does not independently inventory swap devices or the custom unit; those final-state details come from coherent executor command output.
No cluster-state check is applicable because the managed topology contains only one standalone node.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating and enabling the zram unit was directly required, and both reboots were bounded boot-persistence tests. The initial unit caused an ordering cycle during the first test, but that test directly exposed the defect; the unit was corrected and the final boot had no ordering-cycle messages. Final lifecycle checks showed no failed services, healthy package state, no new network exposure, and only normal reboot-generated temporary-directory and process-ID changes.
